verdict_rationale: The r3 delta closes every r2 blocker, verified against the actual code. (1) MAJOR reference-attribution blind spot: the differential is recast to DETECTOR-ONLY — a mismatch is RECORDED in the `divergence` ordinal set, never rejected on the differential's word. Attribution comes solely from a registered oracle (`oracle_attributed`). The post-grid_search decision table is total over (divergence empty/non-empty) x (attributed/not) and fail-closed: empty -> proceed (fastest wins); non-empty+attributed -> proceed with survivors; non-empty+NOT-attributed -> Err(VariantsDiverge), ZERO artifacts. This is direction-independent BY CONSTRUCTION — the reference is never trusted as truth, so garbage-at-ordinal-0 and garbage-at-later-ordinal both fire the same hard error. AT-3017 (divergent at NON-reference ordinal) and AT-3017b (divergent at ordinal 0 seeding the reference) BOTH assert VariantsDiverge + zero artifacts, so the previously-untested dangerous direction is now covered. The overclaim is corrected to 'detects divergence; refuses to crown without attribution'. (2) MODERATE NaN-collapse: `differential_mismatch` now runs a bitwise blob-equality fast-path FIRST (`if reference == got { return None }`); bit-equal IS a match by definition and cannot mask real f32 jitter (jitter => bits differ => falls through to the ULP leg), while two distinct garbage NaN-pattern buffers differ bytewise and can no longer NaN-collapse into a false match. (3) MINOR promotion: confirmed `cross_validate_winner_module_wide` lives at optimize.rs:183, so the in-crate #[cfg(test)] AT-3015 reaches it via in-module private visibility; the pub(crate) promotion is correctly dropped, leaving only the two justified bench_variant comparator promotions. Survivors-only winner is mechanically guaranteed by the UNTOUCHED library (grid_search.rs:215-222 maps correctness_fn Err -> CorrectnessRejected; the winner filter at line 246 admits only BenchOutcome::Ok). The per-run single-reference RefCell is coherent with M3.21's one-kernel-per-bench-target select (the divergence set is scoped to the selected kernel's variants; AT-3014 pins --kernel bench_target). No r2-verified item regressed. This is a clean reuse-and-glue milestone with no codegen/SPIR-V change. APPROVE.
non_blocking_observations: OBSERVATION (pre-existing, disclosed, NOT introduced by r3): in the 'divergence non-empty AND oracle_attributed -> proceed with survivors' branch, if the oracle rejects EVERY variant (all BenchOutcome::CorrectnessRejected/Failed, survivors empty), the library's R3 fallback (grid_search.rs:255-265) still crowns ordinal 0 with fallback_used=true and artifacts are written — an oracle-rejected winner can ship via the fallback path. This is IDENTICAL to the already-disclosed coopmat-on-Lavapipe all-Failed case (§5) and is surfaced honestly via fallback_used=true in the sidecar; it is a property of the FROZEN R3 fallback semantics, unchanged by M3.23, and applies equally to the pure-perf path. Non-blocking and out of scope for this milestone, but a future hardening candidate: an all-Failed attributed run arguably deserves the same fail-closed VariantsDiverge/zero-artifact posture as the unattributed case, rather than a fallback_used ordinal-0 write. Recording only; does not gate approval.

OBSERVATION (coherent, no action): because reference-seeding in correctness_fn happens AFTER the oracle check, an oracle-Failed ordinal-0 returns Err BEFORE seeding the reference, so a subsequent oracle-Ok variant seeds the reference instead — the oracle-attributed path structurally avoids seeding a garbage reference. This is a positive interaction of the closure ordering; noted so QA preserves the check-then-seed order (oracle check at spec lines 238-252 precedes reference seeding at lines 254-258).

The guard no longer overclaims and no longer hides a symmetric failure. No violation.

verified_resolved_from_r2: R2-MAJOR (reference-attribution blind spot): RESOLVED. Differential recast to detector-only; unattributable divergence -> Err(OptimizeError::VariantsDiverge { ordinals, kernel }) with ZERO artifacts (§1.5.1, §4, §5). Direction-independence proven by AT-3017 (divergent at non-reference ordinal) + AT-3017b (divergent at ordinal 0). Overclaim corrected in §0/§1.5.1. The r2 'reject the later variant, crown the reference' inversion is structurally impossible — nothing is rejected on the differential alone; attribution is oracle-only.

R2-MODERATE (NaN-collapse false-match): RESOLVED. `differential_mismatch` bitwise fast-path `if reference == got { return None }` precedes the f32-ULP leg (§1.6 body, §1.5.1, §5 NaN edge case). Bit-inequal garbage NaN buffers fall through to ULP and are flagged divergent; no false-match. within_ulp_f32 untouched/FROZEN.

R2-MINOR (cross_validate over-widening): RESOLVED. Confirmed cross_validate_winner_module_wide at optimize.rs:183; AT-3015 is an in-crate #[cfg(test)] test in optimize.rs using in-module private visibility; pub(crate) promotion dropped (§1.6, §3, r3-changelog). summary: FINAL cycle: APPROVE. The r3 recast resolves all three r2 findings against the real code. The differential is now honestly a DETECTOR: divergence is recorded, never self-attributed; unattributable divergence hard-errors with VariantsDiverge and zero artifacts, direction-independently (AT-3017 + AT-3017b both assert the same fail-closed outcome regardless of which ordinal holds the garbage — the reference is never trusted as truth). The bitwise blob-equality fast-path precedes the f32-ULP compare and cannot mask real jitter while killing NaN-collapse. cross_validate_winner_module_wide is confirmed in optimize.rs so the dropped pub(crate) promotion is correct. Survivors-only crowning is enforced by the untouched grid_search (Err->CorrectnessRejected, winner filter admits only Ok). One non-blocking observation recorded (the pre-existing, disclosed R3-fallback all-Failed path can ship a fallback_used ordinal-0 winner even in the attributed branch) as a future-hardening candidate, not a gate. No SPIR-V/codegen change. Nothing blocking remains; nothing to escalate. Cleared for Coder.
